headline: Russia deploys new jet‑UAVs to cripple Ukraine’s power and transport networks
subheadline: Russian Geran‑5 drones used 40 kg shaped‑charge warheads in a multi‑region barrage, knocking out Kyiv’s electricity and water and affecting at least ten Ukrainian oblasts.
lede: Today's intelligence brief highlights a dramatic escalation in the Ukraine‑Russia war and heightened tensions across the Middle East. Russian forces employed new jet‑powered Geran‑5 UAVs with 40 kg shaped‑charge warheads in a massive overnight barrage that crippled power and water supplies in Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Zhytomyr, while a separate FlyDubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Tabuk after an Omani co‑pilot stabbed the Emirati pilot and attempted to crash the aircraft, only to be subdued by Israeli passengers and crew. The incidents underscore a coordinated push by Moscow to degrade Ukrainian infrastructure and a persistent jihadist threat to Israeli aviation, with the UK attributing an Iran‑linked plot against RAF Fairford and Saudi Arabia striking a communications tower in Yemen.

sections.title: Russian UAV Barrage Cripples Ukrainian Infrastructure
sections.body: Russian forces launched a massive overnight barrage using jet‑powered Geran‑5 UAVs equipped with new 40 kg shaped‑charge warheads to destroy high‑voltage pylons and railway bridges across Kyiv and at least ten other Ukrainian regions. The attacks triggered emergency power and water outages in Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Zhytomyr oblasts, while Russian MoD claimed 123 Ukrainian drones were shot down over Russian territory and the Black Sea. Ukraine’s drone production remains crippled by a shortage of turbojet engines, forcing reliance on third‑country procurement, and McDonald’s Ukraine has cut its menu after a Russian strike on a logistics partner’s warehouse.

sections.title: FlyDubai Hijacking Foiled, Saudi Strikes Continue
sections.body: A FlyDubai aircraft en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia after an Omani co‑pilot stabbed the Emirati pilot and attempted to crash the plane, but Israeli passengers and crew subdued the attacker and the co‑pilot was arrested. Israeli Defense Minister Katz labeled the incident a jihadist terror attempt thwarted by passengers, while Prime Minister Netanyahu confirmed the co‑pilot is in Saudi custody and a rescue plane is en route, and FlyDubai suspended all flights to and from Israel pending investigation. The UK asserted strong indications that Iran was behind a foiled attack on RAF Fairford, a claim rejected by Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi, and Iranian General Naghdi claimed Iran’s military budget is only 1 % of the US’s while stating the US and Israel have been at war with Iran for seven months. Separately, Saudi Arabia’s RSAF struck a communications tower in Jabal Qarn al‑Ajam, Amran, Yemen, continuing its campaign against Houthi infrastructure.

sections.title: Intelligence Assessment
sections.body: The convergence of a jihadist‑linked hijacking attempt on an Israeli‑bound Gulf carrier, Iranian‑attributed plots against UK bases, and Saudi strikes in Yemen illustrates a multi‑vector threat environment across air, cyber, and maritime domains. In Ukraine, Russia’s deployment of specialized shaped‑charge UAVs signals an escalation to infrastructure warfare, while Ukraine’s persistent shortage of turbojet engines and logistical disruptions limit its retaliatory capacity.
